title: Furniture, lighting and tableware from China for restaurants, cafés and hotels: how to order
seo_title: Furniture from China for Restaurants and Hotels
description: Sourcing restaurant, café and hotel furniture from China: what is worth importing, how to write the specification, minimum order, delivery times and quality checks.
lead: Sourcing a restaurant, café or hotel from China lets you buy furniture, lighting, tableware and textiles in one shipment directly from factories. Here is what is worth ordering, how to prepare the specification, how long delivery takes and how not to miss your opening date.

body: h2
How HoReCa procurement differs from furnishing an apartment
p

Furnishing an apartment means choosing furniture for one family. Furnishing a restaurant, café or hotel means buying dozens of identical items that carry hundreds of people a day, clean quickly, survive constant moving and still look tidy after a year in service.
p

So different things matter in HoReCa: the chair frame, not just the upholstery; fabric that is easy to clean; light fittings that can be reached for maintenance; tableware you can reorder from the same range. Furnishing a venue is not shopping — it is procurement to a technical brief.
ul
identical items in large quantities — chairs, tables, glasses, towels
durability matters more than fashion
the option to reorder the same range a season or a year later
one consistent style across items from different manufacturers
h2
What is worth importing from China
p

The biggest price difference is on items where retail mark-ups are high and quantities are large. When a venue needs a hundred chairs, fifty light fittings and several hundred glasses, ordering directly from the manufacturer noticeably changes the budget.
ul
dining room furniture: chairs, armchairs, banquettes, sofas, pedestal tables
bar stools and terrace furniture
decorative lighting: woven and fabric pendants, wall lights, floor lamps
technical lighting: track systems, linear profiles, recessed downlights
tableware: plates, cutlery, glassware, decanters, napkins
hotel textiles: towels, bathrobes, bedspreads, throws
sanitary ware, backlit mirrors and bathroom accessories
p

Furniture that has to fit a niche or a specific wall — a bar counter, built-in cabinets, a complex reception desk — is often easier to make locally from site measurements. The best setup for a venue is usually a combination.

h2
The specification is the basis of the order
p

Sourcing from China cannot be done well from catalogue photos. The basis of the order is a specification: a table in which every item has a product code, dimensions, material, colour, quantity and location in the venue. Ideally it is part of the design project — then furniture sizes match the layout and light fittings match the electrical plan.
p

A good venue specification answers a few questions. How many covers are there inside and on the terrace, and how are they arranged? What are the table and chair heights, so the bar stools suit the counter? Which fabrics and finishes can be cleaned daily? What colour temperature is used in the dining room, at the bar and in the toilets? How many sets of tableware and textiles are needed, including a reserve?
p
If there is no design project, we help put the specification together from the floor plans and your concept. More on our [turnkey procurement](/en/turnkey-procurement) page.

h2
Minimum order, delivery times and payment
p

In our catalogue, [Ozdoba (in Ukrainian)](/ozdoba), the minimum order starts at $500. Items can be combined — chairs, lighting and tableware in one order. We do not sell single pieces: we furnish whole properties, so we work with complete sets for a venue.
p

Delivery from China takes 30–60 days. This is critical for the schedule: if furniture is ordered after the renovation is finished, the venue will stand empty while the shipment travels. So we order right after the specification is approved — in parallel with the renovation, so everything arrives before works are complete.
p

Invoices with closing documents are issued for companies registered in Ukraine; invoicing for EU companies is being set up. Catalogue prices are indicative: we confirm the final cost, availability and delivery time for each item after your enquiry. Whether and on what terms we can deliver outside Ukraine is discussed separately for each project.
h2
How venue procurement works
ol
brief: venue type, number of covers, style, budget and opening date
specification with product codes, dimensions, quantities and prices
approval of fabric, finish and colour samples

delivery, acceptance and completeness check
assembly, placement and lighting installation
final styling and handover
p
At every step you have one contact — a manager who runs procurement from the brief to placement. You see the order status and know in advance what arrives when.

h2
Hotels and mini-hotels: what to consider
p

In a hotel the furnishing is repeated in every room, so a mistake in one item multiplies across all rooms. It is worth assembling one sample room first: bed, bedside tables, reading lights, mirror, textiles, bathroom accessories. Once it has been tested in practice, scale it to the whole hotel. This lets you check guest comfort, sockets and lighting, ease of cleaning — and fix details before the big order.
ul
beds and mattresses with easily removable covers
bedside wall lights with their own switch
bedspreads, throws, towels and bathrobes from one range
backlit mirrors with IP protection for bathrooms
a textile reserve for changing linen between guests
h2
How to check quality before shipment
p

The main risk of ordering from far away is receiving something other than expected: a different fabric shade, a thinner frame, other dimensions. This risk is removed not by trusting photos but by procedure. Before mass ordering we approve fabric and finish samples, and for key items a sample of the product itself or detailed photos and videos from the factory.
p

Before a shipment leaves we check quantities, labelling and packaging so that furniture arrives undamaged. On site every item is accepted against the specification: if something does not match what was approved, it shows immediately — not when guests are already seated. That makes sourcing from China predictable rather than a lottery.
p

A venue should also think ahead and order a few spare chairs, lampshades and textile sets. When something breaks or wears out after a year, the replacement will be from the same range, and the dining room will not turn into a collection of mismatched furniture.
h2
Typical mistakes
ul
ordering furniture before the layout is approved — and getting chairs that do not fit between the tables
choosing light fabrics without a protective finish for the dining room
not building delivery time into the schedule and opening without furniture
buying tableware from a range that cannot be reordered
collecting items from different suppliers without a shared specification
